title: Immaculate Conception Cathedral, Comayagua

buildingCutout.basis: The named cathedral and attached ranges in native way 310133177. The model retains the open north patio within the cadastral envelope.

terrainReference.basis: Original plaza-side ground sample beyond the west front and clear of the cathedral roof.

mapIdentity.provider: OpenStreetMap named cathedral structure way and west-front footprint.
mapIdentity.scope: Named cathedral way 310133177 fixes the southwest wall and east and northwest perimeter. The model partitions the compound into sanctuary, single north tower, north courtyard gate, attached chapels and chapter range. Its exposed north courtyard remains open.

note: Original Terrarium elevations fix the plaza contact and rising east ground. The municipality documents the single four-stage clock tower, five domes and carved west frontage. The IHAH archaeology and Mario Felipe Martínez's study document the arrangement of the aisles, courtyard, sacristy and chapel. Crown, stage divisions, individual drapery and most roof heights are estimates.
